newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE DOLLAR DIPS TO 1.50 TO U.S. DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE DOLLAR DIPS TO 1.50 TO U.S. DOLLAR.

text.p: The Singapore dollar dipped briefly to 1.50 to the U.S. dollar on Tuesday after an official of the country's de-facto central bank said the currency's recent exchange rate was appropriate.
The Singapore dollar recovered slightly above 1.50 and then fell back again, dealers said.
The move followed comments by an official of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) at an economic briefing that the Singapore dollar's level was appropriate to what was happening in the market.
The official said the U.S. dollar had been rising in currency markets recently and the Singapore dollar had depreciated by about five percent against the U.S. unit since the start of 1997.
The Singapore dollar was trading at around 1.4850/70 to the U.S. dollar just before the comments. The currency stood at 1.5040/70 at 0115 GMT, dealers said.
